idiom_name: Vec<HashMap<interned Symbol, Def>> as the open-scope stack
implementation_notes: std ships the containers but not the pattern: the usual realization is a Vec<HashMap<Symbol, Def>> used as the open-scope stack (or parent-linked scopes in an arena) with interned symbols (a Symbol newtype over u32 plus a string interner) so keys are Copy and hashing is cheap; define inserts into the last frame, lookup iterates the frames in reverse, and Result or a bool carries duplicate and unresolved findings. What replaces the classic structure is the standard collections plus Rust's ownership discipline - scopes are owned values, the resolver owns them while walking, and later phases receive an immutable arena rather than a live stack. Keep the hand-written resolver for Rust-hosted compilers and tools; rustc's per-namespace rib stacks (Resolver::visit_scopes, arena-backed scopes addressed by IndexVec, separate ribs for types, values, macros and lifetimes) are the production-scale shape of the same idea, mirroring the second variant.
pitfalls: The borrow checker fights a naive resolver: define needs &mut self while a lookup result borrows &self, so resolve to owned values or ids instead of holding references across a definition in the same pass.

Interning ties symbol identity to the interner's lifetime: the arena must outlive the resolver and every stored Def, and the default SipHash is wasteful for small integer ids - use an identity or FxHash-style hasher.

Collapsing name spaces breaks correctness: rustc keeps separate ribs for types, values, macros and lifetimes, so a single map per scope reports false duplicate definitions when a type and a value share a name.

variants.name: rustc-style arena and rib stack
variants.idiom_name: rustc-style rib stack over IndexVec arenas (one rib per namespace)
variants.implementation_notes: rustc's resolver models the same pattern data-oriented instead of with nested maps: resolution runs in phases with a hierarchical, per-namespace rib stack (each scope pushes a Rib and lookups walk from the innermost rib outward), scope data lives in arenas addressed by ids, and Resolver::visit_scopes is the generic outward walk behind identifier resolution. Choosing this variant means ids instead of references (no borrow tangles, cheap to store in the HIR), compact per-namespace ribs, and a resolver that scales to a whole crate. The cost is more machinery before the first symbol is defined, plus id-validity discipline: ids must not outlive the arena generation they came from, and every lookup must filter by namespace or it will find the wrong kind of name.
pitfalls: Ids must be validated by construction: a stale RibId from an earlier expansion or phase resolves against the wrong frame, so ids must not outlive their arena.
Per-namespace ribs duplicate the traversal: a lookup that forgets to filter by namespace finds a type where a value was meant, which is exactly why rustc's scope sets carry the namespace.
